# Additions to Esther Chapter 5 (Addition E) — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus, Additions to Esther E
**Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/ADE_005_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Decision

Like Addition B, this is a royal letter and should read like one — formal, persuasive, and self-serving. But unlike Addition B, this letter is not murderous; it corrects the previous decree. The Greek author has composed it to mirror and reverse the first edict rhetorically. LOGOS provides the base; PNEUMA contributes clarity at structural joints. The remarkable disclosure that Haman was a "Macedonian" (vv. 8, 11) — an ethnic slur used by Persians — must be preserved without editorial softening.

---

*[Addition E: The counter-decree in favor of the Jews. Inserted after Hebrew Esther 8:12.]*

**1** The following is a copy of the letter: "The Great King Artaxerxes sends greetings to the governors of the one hundred and twenty-seven provinces from India to Ethiopia, and to all who are well-disposed toward our affairs.

**2** Many who have been repeatedly honored through the extraordinary generosity of their benefactors have grown arrogant, and sought not only to oppress those subject to our rule, but — unable to bear good fortune — have plotted against the very people who showed them kindness.

**3** Not only have they driven gratitude out of the human race, but, swollen with the boasts of those who know nothing of goodness, they imagined they could escape the ever-watchful judgment of God who hates evil.

**4** Often those placed in positions of authority have been drawn by the persuasive words of trusted friends into complicity with innocent bloodshed, and have found themselves entangled in irreversible misfortune through the malice of deceit.

**5** One need not look only at the ancient stories handed down to us to observe the lying machinations of ill-disposed men; it is enough to look at what has happened wickedly in recent times, before our very eyes.

**6** We are therefore determined to guard better for the future, rendering the kingdom undisturbed and peaceful for all people,

**7** by making the necessary reforms and consistently judging what is brought before us with more equitable decisions.

**8** Haman son of Hammedatha — a Macedonian by birth, foreign to the Persian blood, and estranged from our goodwill — enjoyed our hospitality and received the full benefit of our generosity toward every nation, to the point of being called our father and honored by all as second after the royal throne.

**9** He was unable to restrain his arrogance, and schemed to deprive us of our kingdom and our life.

**10** Through fabricated intrigues and tricks he sought the destruction of Mordecai, our preserver and perpetual benefactor, and of Esther, the blameless queen who is partner in our kingdom — along with their entire nation.

**11** For by these means he thought, once he had stripped us of our allies, to transfer the rule of the Persians to the Macedonians.

**12** But we find that the Jews are not evildoers; they are governed by the most just of laws,

**13** and are sons of the Most High, the great living God, who has guided our kingdom and that of our ancestors in the most excellent manner.

**14** You will therefore do well not to put into effect the letters sent by Haman son of Hammedatha.

**15** The man who devised these things has already been hanged at the gates of Susa with all his household — God, who rules over all, having swiftly given him the judgment he deserved.

**16** Post copies of this letter publicly everywhere,

**17** and allow the Jews to follow their own customs, and assist them, so that on that very day — the thirteenth of the twelfth month, that is Adar — they may defend themselves against those who attack them at the time of their oppression.

**18** For God, who rules all things, has turned this day for the chosen race from one of destruction into one of joy.

**19** Therefore, among your celebrated festivals, keep this day also with all gladness,

**20** so that both now and hereafter it may be for us and for those who are loyal to the Persians a day of salvation, and for those who plot against us a memorial of their own destruction.

**21** Any city or country that does not act in accordance with these things shall be laid waste with fire and fury — rendered not only inaccessible to human beings but utterly loathsome to wild animals and birds, for all time."
